# Code review follow-up

Apply this skill on every pull request review in this repository, not only when
it looks relevant.

Publish the reconciliation record and suggested lessons as top-level pull request
conversation comments. Do not merge the two artifacts into one comment. The pull
request overview is generated by the platform and any custom text placed there is
discarded, so never use the overview to deliver these artifacts.

Read `references/lesson-schema.md` in this skill directory before writing any
lesson YAML. That file is agent guidance only — do not paste it into the pull
request. The lessons comment already carries the install path (where to save each
YAML file); keep that one-line hint in the comment body.

## 0 — Execution trace

This skill records whether it ran, because the review overview cannot carry that
signal. Do both of the following on every review:

- Append this exact line to the body of the first inline comment you post:

  ```
  <!-- ccr-skill: code-review v1 -->
  ```

  If you post no inline comments, skip this marker rather than inventing a
  comment to hold it.

- Attempt the comment posting in Step 4 and Step 5 as soon as those artifacts
  are ready, before generating the review summary. Do not defer the calls to the
  end of the run.

## 1 — Gate

Confirm `.github/instructions/pull-request-review.instructions.md` exists in the
head checkout. If it is missing, stop. Do not post anything.

## 2 — Resolve pull request coordinates

Reuse the same `owner`, `repo`, and `pullNumber` resolution rules as Step 1 of
`.github/instructions/pull-request-review.instructions.md`. Do not invent a
different method.

## 3 — When to post (idempotency)

Before posting, call `pull_request_read` with methods `get_reviews`,
`get_commits`, and `get_comments` for this pull request.

### Reconciliation comment

On a **first pass** (no prior Copilot review), skip the reconciliation comment.

On a **repeat pass**, decide from code history, not from whether a prior
reconciliation comment exists:

1. Take the most recent prior Copilot review's `commit_id` (or `submitted_at` if
   there is no `commit_id`).
2. If any commit landed on the pull request after that review, **post a new**
   reconciliation comment. Earlier reconciliation comments stay; do not edit or
   delete them. The developer needs the updated addressed / unaddressed picture.
3. If the review was re-requested and **no** code changed since that prior
   Copilot review, **do not** post another reconciliation comment.

### Lessons comment

Post a lessons comment only when this pass has at least one **genuinely new**
finding (see Step 5). Do not post a lessons comment that only re-packages
repeats, declines, or previously lesson-ized issues. A finding raised for the
first time in this pull request may get a lesson; a repeat of an earlier Copilot
finding on this pull request may not.

## 4 — Comment A: reconciliation

When Step 3 says to post a reconciliation comment, post one top-level comment
with `add_issue_comment`, using `issue_number` equal to the pull request number.
The body must use this structure from Step 5 of the review procedure, omitting
empty subsections:

```markdown
## Previous Copilot review follow-up

### Addressed
- `path/to/file.go:210` — restatement and evidence.

### Partially addressed
- ...

### Not addressed
- ...

### Declined
- `path/to/file.go:96` — declined by @user: reason.

### No longer applicable
- ...

### Unverified
- ...
```

Keep the record factual. Name who declined each declined finding and their reason.

## 5 — Comment B: lessons (eligible new findings only)

Build lessons only from **genuinely new** findings in this pass:

- Include: new findings that were not in the prior Copilot inventory.
- Exclude: repeats, addressed items, declined items, partially addressed carry-overs,
  unverified items, style nits with no lasting pattern value.

Prefer high-severity or repo-pattern lessons over formatting nits. Cap at **5**
lessons. If there are no eligible findings, skip this comment.

Each lesson must match the schema in `references/lesson-schema.md`. Choose a
category directory such as `go`, `reliability`, `security`, `testing`, `process`,
or another tag that fits.

Post a **separate** top-level comment with `add_issue_comment`. Never combine it
with the reconciliation comment. The opening lines must include the install path
so the developer knows where to save each file. Use this shape:

```markdown
## Suggested lessons for the Rootstock lessons DB

Copy each block into `skills/lessons/<category>/<id>.yaml`, then add a row to
`skills/lessons/README.md`.

<details>
<summary>category / lesson-id (severity)</summary>

```yaml
id: lesson-id
title: Human-readable title
tags:
  - go
  - reliability
severity: high
frequency: 1
trigger_patterns:
  - pattern
problem: |
  What goes wrong.
bad: |
  Bad pattern.
good: |
  Safer pattern.
why: |
  Why this matters, including that it was found on this pull request.
```

</details>
```

## 6 — Write failure fallback

If `add_issue_comment` fails, is missing from the tool list, or write access is
denied:

- Append one line to the body of the last inline comment you post, in this exact
  form, so the failure is visible on the pull request:

  ```
  ccr-skill: add_issue_comment unavailable — <one-line reason>
  ```

- Do not retry.
- Do not claim the comments were posted.
- Do not put the reconciliation or lessons text in the review overview; that text
  is discarded by the platform and the developer will never see it.

## 7 — Constraints

- Never change the pull request overview comment.
- Never commit lesson files into the repository.
- Never post lessons for declined or repeat findings.
- Never paste `references/lesson-schema.md` into the pull request; only emit
  finished lesson YAML cards plus the install-path hint in the lessons comment.
- Never skip a reconciliation comment when code changed since the last Copilot
  review. Never post a reconciliation comment when a re-review found no code
  changes since that review.
